key: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgot him.
s: Closing the chapter, after the butler is restored and the baker hanged as Joseph foretold, Joseph’s plea to be remembered goes unheeded; Rashi, on 40:23, explains that because Joseph relied on the butler to remember him, he was bound to remain two years in prison.
src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Genesis 40:23, Hebrew text of Rosenbaum and Silbermann (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

evidence.words: וישכחהו. לְאַחַר מִכָּאן. מִפְּנֵי שֶׁתָּלָה בוֹ יוֹסֵף לְזָכְרוֹ, הֻזְקַק לִהְיוֹת אָסוּר שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר שָׂם ה' מִבְטַחוֹ וְלֹא פָנָה אֶל רְהָבִים
evidence.gloss: “And he forgot him”: afterwards. Because Joseph hung his hope on him to remember him, he was bound to be imprisoned two years, as it is said: happy is the man who makes the LORD his trust and turns not to the arrogant (Psalm 40:5).

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Genesis 40:23, at [39,23]). Plain sense faithful to 40:14 to 40:23 (butler restored, baker hanged as Joseph interpreted, the plea of 40:14 unheeded), no four-word run from the verse. Rashi on 40:23 (וישכחהו) says exactly this: because Joseph relied on the butler to remember him he was bound (הֻזְקַק) to remain imprisoned two years. Nothing elsewhere in Rashi on chapter 40 alters it. Entry-check ok.
